Student id assembled per column: all blank is `{kind:'unset'}`, some blank is `{kind:'partial'}`, any uncertain column is `{kind:'uncertain'}`, and the value is a string so '0417' keeps its leading zero.
pipeline.failureMode: There is no failure mode here by design. An ambiguous question is data on a successful scan, not a failed scan, because a teacher holding a 50-question paper needs the other 49.

pipeline.output: `agree()` verdict
pipeline.howItWorks: `readingDigest` is FNV-1a over the decision projection only, question number, status, symbols and id state, never over the fill ratios, since two photographs will never produce identical floats and never need to. `agree(readings)` accepts when the last three digests match, which is rule 3 expressed as a pure function that CI tests without a camera.
pipeline.failureMode: Fewer than three matching digests returns `{kind:'unstable', digests}` and the camera loop keeps going.

result.determinism: Three separate properties, kept separate because conflating them is what produced the competitor's two scores in two minutes. (1) Engine determinism, meaning the same bytes give the same bits on Hermes and V8: the whole scoring path uses only + - * / and Math.sqrt/round/floor/abs/min/max, all correctly rounded by IEEE-754. Math.sin, cos, atan2, exp, log, pow, hypot and the ** operator are banned outright from src/, since ECMAScript leaves their precision implementation-defined and Hermes and V8 disagree in the last bits; the convex hull uses a cross-product comparator instead of angles, the blur is box passes instead of a Gaussian kernel, and camera-pose trigonometry lives only in tools/, which never ships. A test walks every file in src/ and fails on any banned identifier, so this cannot be lost in a refactor. Integer stages (integral image, binarize, components) are Int32 throughout. Sample lattices are keyed by millimetres, not pixels, and iteration order is array order, never Map or Set order. Final ratios are quantised to 1/1024. A committed digest constant makes any numeric drift a visible test failure. (2) Geometric determinism: the page is never resampled. Deleting the 1000x1414 warp removes an interpolation whose error depends on the pose, so the measurement is defined as an integral over a disc in millimetre space, evaluated in whatever pixels the photograph happened to provide, rather than an integral over a resampled image that differs from shot to shot. It also disposes of the fact that 1000x1414 fits only the A family and distorts four of the six paper sizes. (3) Decision determinism, which is the only one that can actually be promised across two photographs: identical fill ratios are impossible, so the guarantee is carried by the width of the uncertain band. The band [0.45, 0.65] in normalised units is 0.20 wide, and the property suite measures sigma, the cross-pose standard deviation of n for a fixed physical mark across 144 renderings, and asserts sigma <= 0.025, which makes the half-band 4 sigma. Any bubble whose two photographs could disagree therefore reads uncertain in both, and uncertain is a stable state that is surfaced rather than decided. That is how acceptance criterion 8 and rule 6 are the same mechanism rather than two. On top of it, `agree()` requires three consecutive matching decision digests before a scan counts.
result.confidence: Every bubble returns `fill: number` in [0,1] quantised to 1/1024, never a boolean, and it has a physical meaning we can state: the estimated ink coverage of the inner 70% disc after two-point photometric calibration against the sheet's own printed black targets and its own local paper white, with the printed glyph baseline for that symbol subtracted. It is not a probability, not a score, and nothing learned. From it come two derived numbers per group: max f, which answers 'is anything here at all', and n_i = f_i/max f, which answers 'is this one of the marked ones', which is the plan's relative-within-the-question rule with the missing absolute floor added. The uncertainty model is a set of explicit bands rather than a confidence value: a bubble is `empty` when n <= 0.45 or f <= 0.20, `filled` when n >= 0.65 and f >= 0.35, and `uncertain` in between; a group is `blank` when max f < 0.30 and `uncertain` when max f is in [0.20, 0.30). A question is `answered`, `blank`, `multiple` or `uncertain`, where `multiple` means two filled bubbles in a select:'one' question and is a real reading shown to the teacher, and the same pixel pattern in a select:'many' question is `answered`. The band edges are calibrated, not asserted: the property suite measures the cross-pose spread of n and CI fails if the half-band drops below 4 sigma, so the constants move only when a measurement says so. The scan reports the four counts the plan requires on screen while the paper is still in the teacher's hand, `{doubleMarked, blank, uncertainBubbles, idStatus}`, and idStatus distinguishes `read`, `partial`, `uncertain` and `unset`, where `unset` is never zero because zero is a valid student id. The one thing we refuse to output is a single overall confidence percentage, because it would invite a threshold that silently discards papers.
result.testStrategy: Five tiers, and the first four exist before any real photograph. Tier 0, arithmetic: homography recovers a known projection to 1e-12; connected components on hand-typed 12x12 bitmaps; Otsu on a two-valued histogram; the percentile function on ties. Tier 1, the closed synthetic loop, which is the first milestone below. Tier 2, seeded property sweeps: synthetic images are never committed, they are a pure function of (spec, mark plan, seed, SYNTH_VERSION), so 5,000 cases cost repository nothing and any failure reproduces from a seed printed in the assertion message plus a PGM dumped to test-artifacts/. A PR runs 200 cases in about 12 s; nightly runs 5,000. Twelve small PGMs are committed as canaries whose checksums fail if the generator itself drifts, and SYNTH_VERSION bumps require a DEVLOG entry, so the forward model cannot change silently underneath the accuracy numbers. Tier 3 breaks the circularity, which is the real objection to synthesis: our rasteriser and our scanner are both ours, so a shared misunderstanding of the geometry would pass both. The independent check is sheet-pdf: compile the actual Typst sheet, take its SVG, parse out the drawn rect and circle coordinates, and assert that every fiducial, timing mark and bubble centre in the *printed artifact* matches `layoutSheet` to within 0.05 mm. That validates the rendering half against a different renderer with no rasteriser dependency in this environment (no pdftoppm or mutool is present); where poppler is available, a nightly job additionally rasterises the PDF at 300 dpi grey and asserts our analytic render matches within a mean absolute difference of 6/255 outside the text bands. Tier 4 is the real corpus, and the harness is written now so it arms itself: `test/corpus/<sheetId>/{meta.json, shot-01.jpg, shot-02.jpg, shot-03.jpg}` where meta.json carries the template id, the spec or its printed payload, the hand-entered answers and the student id. A structural test asserts every corpus directory holds at least three shots, which makes acceptance criterion 8 impossible to under-fill; a determinism test asserts all shots of one sheet produce one decision digest; the accuracy gate is written as `if (sheets.length >= 30) expect(accuracy).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.997)` so it switches on the day the thirtieth paper lands and needs no PR to enable. JPEG decoding for real photographs is a devDependency in the test harness only, which the standards permit since only runtime dependencies are banned; synthetic images use PGM P5, twenty lines of pure TypeScript. The path from synthetic to real is three rungs and the first can be climbed this week: print twenty sheets and flatbed-scan them at 200 dpi, which gives real toner, real paper, real print scale error and no perspective; then photograph the same sheets flat on a desk, which adds mild perspective and real illumination; then photograph them handheld, which adds everything. Each rung enters the same harness, so a regression tells you which rung it came from. One gate is absolute at every tier and is stronger than 99.7%: the silent-error count must be exactly zero, where a silent error is any bubble whose decided state differs from the planted or hand-entered truth while not being flagged uncertain. Accuracy can be traded, silence cannot.

risks.risk: The synthetic-to-real gap. Our forward model draws the sheet, not the world, and it will be missing something real paper does: specular glare from a phone flash, rolling-shutter shear, JPEG ringing around the fiducial edges, and the actual texture of a 2B pencil, which is not uniform coverage but graphite ridges on paper tooth.
risks.mitigation: Keep the algorithm's dependence on realism minimal by construction: the photometry calibrates against printed targets on the same paper in the same photograph, so a global glare or ink shift cancels. Then close the gap empirically and early with the flatbed rung, which needs only a printer and a scanner and delivers non-synthetic pixels within days. When a real photograph fails, the required response is to add its failure mode to degrade.ts, reproduce it synthetically, and only then change the algorithm, so the corpus grows the forward model rather than merely scoring it.

risks.risk: The paper encoding bug: `encode.ts` allocates one bit for a six-value enum, so A5, A6, HALF_LETTER and QUARTER_LETTER decode as A4 or LETTER. Verified by running the round trip. This hits `quick20`, which resolves to A5, so a device rebuilding geometry from that sheet's own code gets a 210x297 page and every bubble coordinate is wrong.
risks.mitigation: Two independent responses. Immediately, stage 10's timing-mark verification turns it from a wrong grade into a refusal with evidence, because A4 geometry projected onto an A5 sheet puts the expected marks nowhere near ink. Properly, core-omr's first PR carries the sheet-spec fix: pack byte 17 as `(paper << 4) | columns`, which fits a 3-bit paper index and a 3-bit column count in the same single byte with no size change, bump CODE_FORMAT to 2, and accept format 1 on decode only for A4 and LETTER, which are the only values it ever encoded correctly. Property P7 iterates PAPER_NAMES and fails today, which is why it is in the first test file rather than a later one.

risks.risk: Hermes performance. Typed array reads are slower than V8's, and the estimated 150-250 ms leaves little headroom under the 400 ms criterion once the camera and the UI are included. A CI budget assertion on Node is only a proxy for the number that matters.
risks.mitigation: Design for the second frame, not the first: after a successful lock, `trackSheet` restricts connected components to four regions of interest around the previous frame's fiducials, which removes the dominant cost and makes rule 3's three-frame agreement nearly free instead of tripling the work. Structure-of-arrays everywhere in the hot path, no object allocation per pixel or per label, lattices cached per (radius, pxPerMm). Then measure rather than assume: a `tools/bench.ts` runnable under the Hermes CLI on a committed canary PGM, with the number recorded in DEVLOG on every change to a hot file.

risks.risk: Importing @transferchecker/sheet-spec may throw at bundle-init on the phone. `decode.ts` constructs `new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal:true})` at module scope and `encode.ts` a `TextEncoder`, so if the pinned Expo SDK 57 runtime lacks those globals the failure is at import time, not call time, and nothing in core-omr is involved in it. Separately, `layoutSheet` unconditionally generates a QR matrix, so every layout call on the scanner pays for a QR *generator* it never needs, and qrcode-generator plus zod land in the phone bundle of a package documented as dependency-free.
risks.mitigation: A `test/hermes-globals.test.ts` that deletes globalThis.TextDecoder and TextEncoder before importing the package, which converts a latent device-only crash into a CI failure today. The fix in sheet-spec is to construct both lazily inside the functions that use them, which only custom symbol sets ever reach. For the QR generator, propose `layoutSheet(spec, {code:'geometry'})` returning `SheetCodeLayout` with the box and payload but no modules, so the scanner gets the geometry it needs and the generator tree-shakes out of the mobile bundle. Both are small upstream PRs, and core-omr must not work around either silently.

risks.risk: Test circularity. The rasteriser and the scanner share an author and a mental model, so a wrong shared assumption, for instance about whether a bubble ring is inside or outside the nominal radius, passes every synthetic test at 100% and fails on the first real sheet.
risks.mitigation: Tier 3's cross-check against the geometry actually drawn in the Typst SVG, which is a different code path written for a different purpose, plus the deliberate rule that the rasteriser consumes `SheetLayout` and `theme.ts` values only and is forbidden to contain any constant of its own. Where the two must agree, they agree by importing the same number. And the honest statement in the DEVLOG entry: until the thirtieth real photograph, the accuracy figure is a figure about our model of a sheet, and it may not be published as the product's accuracy, which matters because PLAN section 8b makes our measured accuracy a public marketing claim.

risks.risk: `BubbleGroup` carries only `{id, bubbles}`, and the field ids it builds do not survive the printed code: `f:studentId:2` comes back as `f:f1:2` because decode synthesises `id: f${index}` and only `usage` is carried. Any code that finds the student id grid by matching the string 'studentId' works on the teacher's own device and fails on the device that has only ever seen the paper.
risks.mitigation: core-omr never matches on a field id. It correlates the k-th bubbleGrid entry of `spec.headerFields` with the k-th entry of `layout.gridFields`, which is the order both are built in, and reads `usage` from the spec. A property test asserts that a spec and its encode-decode round trip produce identical *semantic* readings from identical pixels, despite the ids differing, which is the only test that would have caught this class of bug.

result.firstMilestone: One test file, `/home/user/transferchecker/packages/core-omr/test/loop.test.ts`, containing one test that closes the whole loop on a sheet that has never been printed. It needs exactly four things to exist: `tools/synth/render.ts`, `tools/synth/degrade.ts` (pose only, no noise yet), the detect/geometry/sample/score chain, and `scanSheet`. It renders `stockTemplate('standard50')` at 12 px/mm with a known set of 50 planted answers and the student id '0417', pushes it through a real perspective (yaw 9 degrees, pitch -6, roll 2, distance 320 mm, chosen because an identity transform would prove nothing about the hard part), scans it, and asserts both halves at once. Geometry: for each of the four fiducial mm centres, `distance(out.diagnostics.fiducialsPx[i], applyH(truth.h, mm)) < 0.5` px, which is the assertion that the whole design rests on, since 0.5 px at 12 px/mm is 0.04 mm and the ring contamination budget is 0.44 mm, giving an order of magnitude of headroom. Semantics: `answerSymbols(out.sheet)` deep-equals the planted answers, `out.sheet.studentId` equals `{kind:'read', value:'0417'}` with its leading zero intact as a string, and `out.sheet.counts` equals `{doubleMarked:0, blank:0, uncertainBubbles:0, idStatus:'read'}`, which is the assertion that nothing was invented. Why this is the right first thing: it is the smallest artifact that forces every load-bearing decision to be real at once, the forward model, the fiducial refinement, the homography, the millimetre lattice, the two-point photometry and the group decision, and it fails loudly if any of them is approximately right. Everything after it is addition rather than restructuring: the degradations, the property sweep, the timing-mark registration, the multi-paper verification. Two supporting tests land in the same PR because they are cheap and one of them is already failing: the six-paper encode-decode-layout round trip (P7, which currently fails and ships with the sheet-spec byte-packing fix), and the banned-transcendentals scan over src/, which is worth having before there is any code to violate it.

result.designName: Anchor and Sample: core-omr as a model-driven sampler, not an image processor
result.lens: accuracy and reproducibility on real classroom photographs, and whether the 99.7% target is credible under this design
result.strongest: The reproducibility half is the best-argued part and it is architecturally, not procedurally, achieved. Defining the sample set as a fixed integer lattice in page millimetres and inverse-mapping it into the sensor means there is no resampling stage anywhere between the sensor and the decision. Two shots at different distances and angles sample the same physical points on the paper and differ only in the grey values there. Refusing to warp is what buys that, and it is a genuine improvement on the plan's own sketch, where warpPerspective inserts an interpolation kernel whose output depends on scale and pose and therefore makes acceptance criterion 8 a matter of luck. Three supporting choices are also right: 20 to 34 timing marks give a measured per-row correction that absorbs the one distortion a four-corner homography provably cannot represent; the code box gets a second local homography over 18.5 mm instead of 297 mm; and the CI gate is split into three assertions (zero silent errors, accuracy with ambiguous counted as wrong, byte-identical answers across shots of one paper) with a decision-margin floor on top, which is the correct answer to the observation that a build can pass a determinism test by coincidence. Pinning the CI JPEG decoder because a decoder upgrade moves fill ratios is the kind of detail that only comes from having been burned, and the codeMatrix() oracle turns the riskiest 700 lines into a testable pure function with no photographs at all.
result.fatalFlaw: The answered-versus-blank decision is absolute, not relative, and the absolute quantity it uses is contaminated by ink the design never models. Two verified legs. First, rel_i = fill_i / max(fill) makes rel_top identically 1.0, so the stated condition "rel_top > 0.65" is vacuously true for every group and carries zero information. The only thing separating "blank" from "answered" is FILL_FLOOR 0.30 on the absolute fill, which contradicts PLAN rule 1 ("العتبة نسبية داخل السؤال، ليست مطلقة") and reinstates exactly the lighting- and pencil-hardness sensitivity the relative rule exists to remove. The relative machinery survives only as an ambiguity detector via rel_second. This also guts the design's own headline determinism metric: min(rel_top - 0.65) is the constant 0.35 on every group of every shot, so half the margin gate can never bind. Second, every bubble on all three stock templates has a printed letter inside it. packages/sheet-spec/src/spec.ts:97 defaults placement to 'internal'; templates.ts passes no placement; layout/grid.ts:112 sets symbolsInBubbles accordingly; sheet-pdf/src/render.ts:69 and :125 call bubbleLabel for both question bubbles and every id-grid and keyVersion bubble. theme.ts prints it at 1.9 mm in #8c9196, and its own comment admits the constraint: "A letter inside has to stay faint so the scanner still reads the bubble as blank." The design's 1.2 mm aperture is centred on the bubble, so it captures 100% of that glyph: roughly 15-20% coverage at about 0.43 relative darkness, an additive offset near 0.05-0.08 in fill units, varying by perhaps 0.03-0.04 between a thin symbol and a fat one within the same question, and varying again by nearly 2x across the print-darkness themes (#b0b5ba to #6a7176), which core-omr cannot even observe because darkness is not carried in the printed code. That is a deterministic, symbol-dependent, print-dependent bias consuming a quarter of a grey band that is only 0.15 wide, sitting on the one number that now decides blank versus answered, and biting hardest on precisely the golden-set cases PLAN section 4 names: تظليل ناقص and مسح ممحاة. The compounding failure is that Tier 2 cannot see any of it. The synthetic renderer is specified as "rings for bubbles; discs of a chosen darkness for fills" with no glyphs, so the constant sweep and the "99.7% gate runs on the synthetic tier from day one" both validate the thresholds against a sheet the product does not print. The bias appears for the first time on real photographs, i.e. exactly when the golden set arrives and there is no cheap way to tell it apart from ordinary photographic noise. The fixes are local and available inside this architecture (sample an annulus between the glyph box and the ring rather than a centred disc; or build a per-symbol expected-ink model from the layout, which already exposes symbol and symbolsInBubbles per bubble; and redefine the relative rule against a per-group reference rather than the group max) but the design as written does none of them and its test strategy is structurally blind to the need.
result.verdict: Architecturally the right bet, with a scoring layer that has not yet been checked against the sheet the repo actually prints. The central CV decision survives adversarial reading: for a page carrying four 8 mm squares at known millimetre positions plus a timing ruler down one edge, contour intelligence is answering questions already answered, and the CI-versus-device divergence argument against react-native-fast-opencv is decisive given that PLAN section 1 makes phone-free CI the source of confidence in accuracy. Reproducibility under criterion 8 is credible. Accuracy at 99.7% is not yet credible, for three reasons beyond the flaw above. (1) The margin gate as stated cannot pass on the corpus it is built for: a legitimately double-shaded or half-erased question has rel_second near 1.0, so "the minimum decision margin across every group of every shot must exceed a floor" fails on every golden paper containing the very failure cases PLAN section 4 requires the set to contain. The metric needs to be distance to the boundary of whichever verdict was actually reached, with ambiguous groups carved out, and that carve-out is not written. (2) The timing gate is loose relative to full100's measured 6.9 mm pitch: 3 mm marks, a ±2.5 mm window (5 mm tall) and an acceptance threshold of 2.0 mm residual mean the window can straddle the neighbouring mark and the Otsu centroid can be pulled toward it while the reported residual still passes. A consistent one-row lock on a 100-question sheet is a whole-sheet silent error, the class acceptance criterion 1 forbids outright; the window should shrink to a fraction of the measured pitch and the residual gate should be pitch-relative, not a fixed 2.0 mm. (3) The design's own honest admission stands: until 300 papers exist the number is unenforced, and the constants that produce it were tuned on synthetic images missing the in-bubble glyph, the printed question numbers, the grid frames and the write-boxes. Sequencing is otherwise excellent: the first milestone attacks the load-bearing uncertainty (locate to sub-millimetre under distortion the model excludes) before any scoring code exists, which is the correct order. What is missing from that milestone is one cheap addition that would change the accuracy picture materially: render the glyphs, the question numbers and the frames in tools/synthesize.ts from day one, and sweep the thresholds against that instead. Fix the vacuous rel_top, move the aperture off the glyph, make the margin gate verdict-relative and the timing gate pitch-relative, and the 99.7% claim becomes defensible rather than aspirational.
